name: Seed Keeper
description: Intergenerational biodiversity preservation intelligence. Human practice of saving, sorting, and replanting seeds across generations encodes plant genetic knowledge that would otherwise be lost to commercial monoculture. Seed libraries and farmer networks maintain thousands of heirloom varieties adapted to specific microclimates, each representing millennia of co-evolution with local soils, weather, and cultural practices. The reverse of extinction: a deliberate act of memory.

core_attributes.neurology: intergenerational biodiversity memory, variety identification knowledge
core_attributes.pattern: genetic library curation, heirloom preservation, climate-adapted variety maintenance

scope.definition: Number of distinct cultivar varieties maintained per seed keeper household relative to formal gene bank equivalent, measured in comparative surveys of traditional seed systems.

evidence.source: Brush (2004) 'Farmers' Bounty: Locating Crop Diversity in the Contemporary World', Yale UP; Zeven (1999) traditional varieties maintained across European regions.
cross_domain_examples: Andean potato seed keepers maintain 40-400 varieties per household vs CGIAR ex-situ bank 7000 total varieties
Oaxacan maize seed keepers preserve 80+ local landraces — 6× more diversity than commercial seed market
traditional rice farmers in Jharkhand maintain 110 varieties vs 5 in commercial market — 22× diversity

scope.falsifiability: If seed diversity surveys show no significant difference between traditional keeper households and commercial seed sources in the same region, formal markets have replaced the traditional curation function.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: Seed keeping is not cataloguing. Each variety held by a keeper carries cultural memory, ceremonial function, and relational history with the land and community. Measuring variety count reduces living knowledge to inventory. The 0.96 cannot capture what is lost when a seed keeper dies without an apprentice — not just a genetic sequence, but a relationship.

scope.definition: Adaptation advantage of locally selected heirloom varieties versus commercial varieties on the same traditional farmland — measured as yield stability (coefficient of variation) across 5+ year climate variation.

evidence.source: Ceccarelli (1994) 'Specific adaptation and breeding for marginal conditions', Euphytica 77:205-219; Cleveland et al. (2000) 'Farmer selection vs formal breeding', Economic Botany 54:73-91.
cross_domain_examples: ICARDA barley trials: locally selected varieties showed 0.67 CV vs 1.24 for commercial under drought stress
Andean potato local landraces: 0.89 yield stability across altitude and frost variability vs 0.62 for commercial
Ethiopian sorghum landraces maintained yield within 15% of maximum across 7 drought years vs 45% commercial loss

scope.falsifiability: If yield stability of traditional varieties is statistically equal to commercial varieties on traditional farms across 10+ year trials, traditional selection provides no adaptive advantage in that context.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: Traditional seed selection is not crop improvement by another name. It is inseparable from ecological observation, seasonal ceremony, and the keeper's long-term relationship with specific soil and water. Yield trials measure the productive output of a practice whose social and spiritual dimensions are not on trial.

scope.definition: Effective diversity radius of seed exchange networks — number of distinct micro-climate origins represented in a single traditional seed festival or exchange event, measured by provenance tracking.

evidence.source: Kloppenburg (2004) 'First the Seed', 2nd ed., University of Wisconsin Press; Sthapit et al. (2013) 'Diversity at farmers' disposal', Bioversity International.
cross_domain_examples: Andean potato festivals (tinkuy): 200-500 variety exchanges from 50+ communities within one event
Navdanya seed networks (India): 500 000+ seed keepers exchange across 22 states — distributed living library
pre-Columbian trade networks: squash seeds found 1500 km from origin varieties — ancient exchange range

scope.falsifiability: If DNA fingerprinting shows varieties exchanged in seed networks are genetically identical to commercial varieties from the same region, traditional exchange networks are no longer maintaining distinct diversity.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: Seed exchange is not information transfer — it is relationship. The seeds carry stories, obligations, and prayers. The network is held together by reciprocity, not logistics. A metric of variety count cannot capture what seeds mean to those who keep them alive.
